exposure: single umbilical artery with associated pathologies
presence or absence of single umbilical artery
finding: Singleton pregnancies complicated with single umbilical artery (SUA) had significantly poorer perinatal outcomes, including higher rates of C-section, premature delivery, low birth weight, and fetal malformations.
mod_finding: The study found that Cesarean section was performed more frequently in cases with a single umbilical artery compared to those without (40 cases with SUA vs. 5258 without SUA).
